readme:
# NTRO Signal Analyzer

GUI-based automated analysis tool for **.IQ** and **.wav** terrestrial signals (HF/VHF/UHF).

## Features

1. **Parameter extraction** — sampling rate, bandwidth, SNR, modulation estimate, FEC/interleaving inference
2. **Visualizations** — spectrum, waterfall, constellation, I/Q time domain
3. **Demodulation** — BPSK, QPSK, 16-QAM, FSK
4. **De-interleaving** — Block, Convolutional, Diagonal, Pseudo-random
5. **FEC** — Viterbi (K=7), RS block, LDPC, Concatenated
6. **Bit stream correlation** — preamble/header search and payload preview

## Setup

```bash
cd signal-analyzer
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## Run

```bash
python main.py
```

## Demo

1. Click **Load File** and select a `.wav` or `.IQ` file.
2. For `.IQ` files, set sample rate and format (`cf32`, `ci16`, `cu8`).
3. Use tabs 1–6 or click **Run Full Pipeline** for end-to-end analysis.

**Architecture diagram (one slide):** open `docs/architecture-slide.html` in a browser and screenshot, or use the Mermaid diagram in `docs/architecture-slide.md`.

Generate sample files (optional):

```bash
python -c "from demo_signals import *; generate_qpsk_wav('demo.wav'); generate_fsk_iq('demo.iq'); print('Created demo.wav and demo.iq')"
```

## Note

This is an **ideation-round prototype**. Parameter/FEC inference uses heuristics suitable for demonstration; production systems would use trained classifiers and full protocol stacks (e.g. GNU Radio).

readme:
# Signal Analyzer

> **End-to-end RF signal inspection, automatic modulation classification, demodulation, synchronization, and Forward Error Correction (FEC) decoding — built as the software solution for SIH 2026 Problem Statement #26147.**

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Problem Statement](#problem-statement)
2. [Features](#features)
3. [Screenshots](#screenshots)
4. [Project Structure](#project-structure)
5. [Installation](#installation)
6. [Usage](#usage)
7. [Sample Files](#sample-files)
8. [Running Tests](#running-tests)
9. [Keyboard Shortcuts](#keyboard-shortcuts)
10. [License](#license)

---

## Problem Statement

**SIH 2026 — Problem #26147**

Design a software tool that can:
- Accept raw I/Q captures (`.iq`, `.bin`, `.wav`) from any SDR front-end.
- Automatically identify the modulation scheme without prior knowledge.
- Demodulate the baseband bitstream with carrier/timing compensation.
- Locate frame synchronisation markers and resolve phase ambiguities.
- Blind-detect and apply Forward Error Correction to recover the information payload.
- Present spectrum, waterfall, and constellation visualisations in a single operator console.

---

## Features

| Category | Capability |
|---|---|
| **Modulation Classification** | Random-Forest classifier using higher-order cumulants (C₄₀, C₄₂), envelope kurtosis, spectral symmetry — supports **BPSK, QPSK, 16QAM, 2FSK** with confidence scoring |
| **Demodulation** | Optimal carrier frequency offset (CFO) correction, Gardner/Mueller-Müller symbol timing recovery, Gray-coded constellation demapping |
| **Visualisation** | Interactive PSD spectrum, waterfall/spectrogram, and I/Q constellation plots rendered with Matplotlib embedded in PySide6 |
| **Frame Synchronisation** | Cross-correlation sync-word search (default `0xEB902A3C`, CCSDS `0x1ACFFC1D`, custom); dual-check noise-floor guard; phase-ambiguity resolution (0°/180°/90°/270°) |
| **FEC Auto-Detection** | Blind identification across Reed-Solomon (RS-64,48 / RS-32,24), LDPC (128,64 Rate-½), Concatenated RS+Viterbi, and Convolutional K=7 Rate-½ with four de-interleaver architectures |
| **FEC Decoding** | Error-correction with re-encode match metric and ground-truth BER for synthetic test files |
| **Export / Reporting** | JSON & CSV data export; single-page PDF report with metrics table + spectrum + waterfall |
| **Rate Estimation** | Cyclostationary baud-rate auto-estimation on file load with suggested Fₛ override |

---

## Screenshots

### Spectrum View — BPSK Signal

![BPSK Power Spectral Density](docs/bpsk_spectrum.png)

### Constellation View — BPSK & 2FSK

| BPSK | 2FSK |
|---|---|
| ![BPSK Constellation](docs/bpsk_constellation.png) | ![2FSK Constellation](docs/2fsk_constellation.png) |

### Spectrum View — QPSK & 2FSK

| QPSK PSD | 2FSK PSD |
|---|---|
| ![QPSK Spectrum](docs/qpsk_spectrum.png) | ![2FSK Spectrum](docs/2fsk_spectrum.png) |

---

## Project Structure

```
signal_analyzer/
├── main.py                  # CLI entry point (GUI + headless modes)
├── requirements.txt
├── samples/                 # Curated .iq starter files (see below)
├── docs/                    # Screenshots used in this README
│
├── gui/
│   ├── main_window.py       # PySide6 main window (~3 000 lines)
│   └── style.qss            # Dark-mode Qt stylesheet
│
├── modulation/
│   ├── classifier.py        # Feature extraction + Random Forest
│   ├── classifier_model.joblib   # Pre-trained model (ships with repo)
│   ├── demodulator.py       # BPSK/QPSK/16QAM/2FSK demod
│   ├── fec.py               # FEC orchestrator
│   ├── fec_identifier.py    # Blind FEC detector
│   ├── correlator.py        # Sync-word cross-correlator
│   ├── ldpc.py              # LDPC Min-Sum BP decoder
│   ├── rs_fec.py            # Reed-Solomon GF(2⁸) codec
│   ├── concatenated.py      # Concatenated RS+Viterbi codec
│   ├── deinterleaver.py     # Block / convolutional / diagonal de-interleavers
│   └── signal_gen.py        # Synthetic signal generator (training data)
│
├── dsp/
│   ├── spectrum.py          # Welch PSD analysis
│   ├── waterfall.py         # Short-time FFT waterfall
│   ├── constellation.py     # I/Q scatter plot
│   └── rate_estimator.py    # Cyclostationary baud-rate estimator
│
├── sig_io/
│   └── iq_reader.py         # Multi-format IQ/WAV loader
│
└── correlation/             # Low-level correlation utilities
```

---

## Installation

### Prerequisites

- **Python 3.11 or 3.12** (3.13 not yet tested with PySide6 6.x)
- A virtual environment tool (`venv` or `conda`)

### Steps

```bash
# 1. Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/<YOUR_USERNAME>/signal-analyzer.git
cd signal-analyzer

# 2. Create and activate a virtual environment
python -m venv .venv

# Windows
.venv\Scripts\activate

# macOS / Linux
source .venv/bin/activate

# 3. Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

> **Note for Linux users**: PySide6 requires `libGL` and `libEGL`.
> Install with: `sudo apt install libgl1 libegl1`

---

## Usage

### Launch the GUI

```bash
python main.py
```

**With a file pre-loaded at startup:**

```bash
python main.py samples/bpsk_1000ksps_f32.iq
```

### Full Pipeline Walkthrough

1. **Open File** — Click *Open File* (`Ctrl+O`) or drag-and-drop a `.iq` / `.wav` file onto the window. Select the sample rate (defaults to 1 MHz for raw `.iq`).
2. **Classify** — Click *Classify Modulation* to identify the scheme (BPSK / QPSK / 16QAM / 2FSK) with confidence %.
3. **Demodulate** — Click *Demodulate* to recover the raw bitstream with CFO and timing correction.
4. **Find Sync** — Select a sync word from the dropdown and click *Find Sync*. Phase ambiguity is resolved automatically.
5. **Auto-Detect FEC** — Click *Auto-Detect FEC*. The blind analyzer tests RS, LDPC, Concatenated, and Convolutional families.
6. **Decode** — Click *Decode* (`Ctrl+D`) to apply the detected FEC and view the corrected payload in the Bitstream tab.
7. **Export** — Use *Export Data* (JSON/CSV) or *Save Report* (PDF/PNG) in the right sidebar.

### Headless / Batch Mode (No GUI)

Generate spectrum + waterfall + constellation PNGs for all three sample signals:

```bash
python main.py --headless all
# or for a single signal:
python main.py --headless bpsk
python main.py --headless qpsk
python main.py --headless 2fsk
```

Plots are saved to `samples/<name>_spectrum.png`, `..._waterfall.png`, `..._constellation.png`.

---

## Sample Files

Three curated `.iq` files are included in `samples/` so you can try the tool immediately without an SDR:

| File | Modulation | Sample Rate | Size |
|---|---|---|---|
| `samples/bpsk_1000ksps_f32.iq` | BPSK | 1 Msps | 128 KB |
| `samples/qpsk_1000ksps_f32.iq` | QPSK | 1 Msps | 128 KB |
| `samples/2fsk_1000ksps_f32.iq` | 2FSK | 1 Msps | 128 KB |

**Format**: Interleaved IEEE-754 float32 (I, Q, I, Q, …), no header — identical to GNU Radio `File Sink` with `float` type.

To generate additional test signals (with FEC payloads, sync words, etc.) see the generator scripts in `samples/generate_*.py` and the guide at [`GUIDE_generating_test_signals.md`](GUIDE_generating_test_signals.md).

---

## Running Tests

```bash
# Modulation classifier
python -m pytest test_demod.py -v

# FEC pipeline (RS, LDPC, Concatenated, Convolutional)
python -m pytest test_fec.py test_rs_pipeline.py test_ldpc.py -v

# Frame synchronisation regression
python verify_sync_regression.py

# All tests
python -m pytest -v
```

---

## Keyboard Shortcuts

| Shortcut | Action |
|---|---|
| `Ctrl + O` | Open signal file |
| `Ctrl + D` | Execute FEC Decode |
| `Ctrl + R` | Reset application state |
| `1` | Spectrum tab |
| `2` | Waterfall tab |
| `3` | Constellation tab |
| `4` | Bitstream tab |
| `Esc` | Dismiss alert banners |

---

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details.

IQ signal ingestion - WAV signal ingestion - Signal pre-processing - Spectrum / PSD analysis - Waterfall visualization - Constellation visualization - SNR estimation - Bandwidth estimation - Symbol-rate estimation - Carrier-offset estimation - Modulation analysis - Digital signal demodulation - Bitstream generation and recovery - Bitstream correlation - Frame-boundary detection - Interleaver detection - De-interleaving - FEC detection and decoding - Recovered bitstream analysis --- ## Supported Modulation SignalSight currently implements and validates: - BPSK - QPSK - 8PSK - 2FSK / BFSK - 16QAM - 64QAM The modulation processing is scoped to the supported configuration space. --- ## Supported FEC The current implementation includes: - Viterbi - Reed-Solomon - Concatenated Viterbi + Reed-Solomon - LDPC The LDPC implementation is scoped to the validated `(256,128)` regular-code configuration with min-sum belief-propagation decoding. --- ## Supported De-interleaving SignalSight implements: - Block de-interleaving - Convolutional de-interleaving - Diagonal de-interleaving - Pseudo-random de-interleaving --- ## Signal Parameter Extraction The system estimates and extracts important signal parameters including: - Sample rate - Signal-to-noise ratio - Bandwidth - Symbol rate - Carrier-frequency offset These parameters are used by the subsequent signal-processing stages. --- ## Signal Visualization SignalSight provides an integrated visualization workspace containing: ### Spectrum / PSD Frequency-domain representation of the input signal for spectral analysis. ### Waterfall Time-frequency visualization for observing signal behavior over time. ### Constellation Complex-symbol visualization for supported PSK and QAM modulation schemes. ### Bitstream Recovered bits can be inspected after demodulation, correlation, de-interleaving and FEC processing. --- # Application Screenshots SignalSight provides an integrated desktop workbench for signal analysis, visualization, demodulation, de-interleaving, FEC processing and bitstream recovery. ## Signal Overview The Overview workspace displays the detected modulation, estimated SNR, bandwidth, symbol rate, signal information and processing status in a single interface. --- ## Power Spectral Density The Spectrum workspace provides a frequency-domain representation of the input signal for analysing its spectral characteristics and occupied bandwidth. --- ## Waterfall / Spectrogram The Waterfall workspace provides a time-frequency representation of the signal for observing signal activity and frequency behaviour over time. --- ## Constellation Analysis The Constellation workspace visualizes the complex I/Q symbols in the signal, providing a graphical representation of supported digital modulation characteristics. --- ## Recovered Bitstream The Bit Stream workspace displays the recovered binary data after demodulation, bit correlation, de-interleaving and FEC processing. The recovered data can be viewed in binary or hexadecimal representation. --- # Processing Pipeline ```text IQ / WAV Input | v Signal Parsing | v Pre-processing | v Spectral Analysis | v Parameter Extraction | v Modulation Analysis | v Demodulation | v Bitstream Generation | v Bit Correlation / Frame Alignment | v Interleaver Analysis | v De-interleaving | v FEC Processing | v Recovered Bitstream

readme:
# 📡 NTRO Signal Intelligence Workstation (SIH 2026 — SIH26147)
### Autonomous RF Parameter Extraction and Modulation Recognition Suite

**Sponsoring Organization:** National Technical Research Organisation (NTRO)  
**Problem Statement ID:** SIH26147  
**Theme:** Smart Automation / Software  
**Domain:** Electronics & Communication Engineering (ECE) / Signals Intelligence (SIGINT)  
**Architecture Edition:** v4.1 (Blind Physical Measurement + Epistemic Validation Engine)

---

## 🧭 Project Overview & Engineering Rationale

When electronic surveillance pods or signals intelligence (SIGINT) listening posts intercept an unknown radio frequency (RF) transmission, the intercepting operator has **zero prior knowledge** about the transmitter. Traditional communications receivers require an operator to manually configure the carrier frequency, channel filter, and baud rate before any data can be recovered. If the parameters are incorrect, the receiver outputs noise.

```
                           UNKNOWN INTERCEPTED RF SIGNAL
                                         │
                                         ▼
                 ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                 │       "What physical signal is this?"         │
                 │   "What are its carrier, baud, and shift?"    │
                 │    "Can we mathematically trust this read?"   │
                 └───────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Why Pure Deep Learning Classifiers Fall Short in Defense SIGINT
Most automated classification attempts rely on deep neural networks trained on synthetic datasets. In operational environments, black-box neural networks present severe failure modes:
1. **Uncalibrated Overconfidence:** Neural networks force a classification label even when fed out-of-distribution noise, soundcard aliasing artifacts, or unfamiliar jamming signals.
2. **Zero Mathematical Explanation:** A neural network cannot produce physical audit trails or state *why* it arrived at an answer.
3. **No Parameter Extraction:** Classifying a signal as "FSK" does not yield carrier frequency, frequency shift ($\Delta f$), modulation index ($h$), or symbol rate ($R_s$).

### Our Core Philosophy: Empirical Physics First
Our workstation enforces a strict physical evidence architecture:
1. **Measure First:** Extract physical parameters directly from the raw waveform (bandwidth, carrier offset, spectral flatness, squaring line prominence, pulse trains) without protocol labels.
2. **Hypothesize Second:** Formulate competing candidate hypotheses from measured physical features.
3. **Challenge the Hypothesis:** Search actively for measurable physical contradictions.
4. **Enforce Validation Gates:** Require multi-window temporal stability and mathematical proofs before promoting any candidate to `VALIDATED`.

---

## 🏛️ System Architecture (Architecture v4.1)

The pipeline is organized into five operational layers:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ LAYER 1: SIGNAL PREPARATION & CONDITIONING                                  │
│   • loaders.py: Autonomous container probing (.wav / .iq / .bin / .sigmf)   │
│   • preprocessor.py: DC bias cancellation, scale-invariant power norm       │
│   • spectral.py: Welch PSD computation, 2D STFT spectrogram waterfall       │
└──────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘
                                       │
┌──────────────────────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────────────┐
│ LAYER 2: BLIND MEASUREMENT & MODULATION INFERENCE                           │
│   • blind_parameter_engine.py: Bandwidth (-3dB/-10dB/99%), Carrier (fc),    │
│     M2M4 SNR, Spectral Flatness, Squaring Lines, Envelope Autocorrelation   │
│   • modulation_inference.py: Modulation family inference (CW, FSK, BPSK,     │
│     QPSK, 8-PSK, QAM, FMOP, GMSK) without catalog lookup                   │
└──────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘
                                       │
┌──────────────────────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────────────┐
│ LAYER 3: CANDIDATE RANKING & TEMPORAL VALIDATION                            │
│   • protocol_inference.py: Knowledge-layer mapping to candidate protocols   │
│   • temporal_validator.py: Multi-window temporal stability & variance test  │
│   • candidate_ranker.py: Multi-candidate ranking with ambiguity detection   │
└──────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘
                                       │
┌──────────────────────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────────────┐
│ LAYER 4: CONTRADICTION ANALYSIS & 6-PILLAR VALIDATION GATE                  │
│   • contradiction_analyzer.py: Active search for physical rule violations   │
│   • validation_gate.py: Physical proof arbitration across 6 strict gates     │
│     (Evidence, Temporal, Duration, Nyquist, Contradiction, Ambiguity)       │
└──────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘
                                       │
┌──────────────────────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────────────┐
│ LAYER 5: ADAPTIVE EXTRACTION, UNCERTAINTY & OPERATOR HUD                    │
│   • adaptive_pipeline.py: Specialized protocol extractors (Radar ΔR/PRF,    │
│     FSK shift/h, TDMA burst clocks, PSK/QAM EVM, Voice formants)            │
│   • parameter_uncertainty.py: Epistemic confidence bounds (k=2, 95% CI)    │
│   • app.py & cli.py: Streamlit real-time HUD and CLI sensor handoff         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### The Six Epistemic States
Every analysis verdict is assigned an explicit epistemic status in `contracts.py`:
* **`VALIDATED`**: The signal satisfies all six validation gates, exhibits high temporal stability, has zero unresolved contradictions, and matches physical modulation criteria.
* **`ESTIMATED`**: Continuous physical parameters are extracted, but the signal displays temporal drift, low SNR, or incomplete code proof.
* **`AMBIGUOUS`**: Multiple candidate hypotheses share overlapping feature bounds (e.g. Bell 202 vs. POCSAG 1200) within a margin of $|\Delta \text{score}| \le 0.05$. Both are preserved.
* **`UNKNOWN`**: Genuine RF energy is detected, but its modulation profile does not match cataloged standards. Raw physical parameters are preserved.
* **`UNKNOWN_OOD`**: The waveform deviates from expected RF feature manifolds (e.g. non-linear chaotic dynamics). Refuses forced misclassification.
* **`NO SIGNAL / NOISE FLOOR`**: The capture contains only stationary receiver thermal noise, rejected at the front-end gate with zero false positives.

---

## 🚀 Quick Start Guide

### 1. Installation
This suite runs on Python 3.10 through 3.14 on Linux, macOS, and Windows.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yoganandasp15/SIH_2026_Signal-Analyser.git
cd SIH_2026_Signal-Analyser
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

### 2. Launch the Interactive GUI Dashboard
On Windows, double-click **`START_DASHBOARD.bat`**, or launch from the terminal:
```bash
streamlit run app.py
```
Open your browser at `http://localhost:8501`.
* **Zero-Config Drag & Drop:** Drop any `.wav`, `.iq`, or raw binary file into the upload zone. The engine automatically probes the byte container, sampling rate, modulation family, and parameters.
* **Preset Intercept Gallery:** Select from 25 real-world defense captures in the sidebar to review instantaneous triage results.
* **Interactive Visualizers:** Switch between Welch PSD, 2D STFT Spectrogram, I/Q Constellation (WebGL accelerated), Eye Diagram, and Time Envelope.
* **Embedded Audio Player:** Listen to demodulated audio directly in the browser via `st.audio`.
* **Telemetry Exporters:** Download full analysis reports in structured JSON or tabular CSV.

### 3. Run Autonomous CLI Processing
Run single-command batch analyses without opening a web browser:
```bash
# Analyze a NAVTEX maritime telex intercept
python cli.py -i verified_samples/NAVTEX.wav

# Analyze an over-the-horizon radar capture
python cli.py -i verified_samples/OTH_SW_Radar.wav

# Process a cellular TDMA capture and export telemetry to JSON and CSV
python cli.py -i verified_samples/GSM_BCCH_Downlink.wav -j gsm_report.json -c gsm_summary.csv

# Generate and benchmark a calibrated synthetic test signal
python cli.py --generate --mod QPSK --snr 15 --fs 2000000 --fc 100000 --save-synth qpsk_test.iq
```

### 4. Run the Automated Test Suite (177 Tests)
Run the full test suite with Python's built-in test runner:
```bash
python -m unittest discover tests
```
All 177 tests run and pass cleanly.

---

## 🔒 Defense & Security Compliance

* **100% Offline & Air-Gapped:** Zero external API calls, zero telemetry phone-home, zero cloud dependencies. Suitable for deployment in air-gapped operations centers and forward SIGINT pods.
* **Zero Licensing Cost:** Built entirely on open-source Python libraries (`numpy`, `scipy`, `pandas`, `plotly`, `streamlit`), replacing high-cost proprietary software licenses.
* **Streaming Memory Guardrails:** Uses chunk-bounded buffer processing and memory-mapped file access, preventing memory exhaustion when inspecting multi-gigabyte SDR captures.
* **Transparent Auditability:** Every classification verdict includes the underlying mathematical equations, measured features, tested hypotheses, rejected alternatives, and confidence intervals.

# SIGINT Tool — Automated Signal Analysis & Parameter Extraction System

> **PS 26147 (NTRO) — Hackathon Prototype**

End-to-end automated signal intelligence tool that ingests raw `.wav` / `.iq` / `.sigmf` recordings and extracts signal parameters, modulation type, decoded bits, and frame structure — with zero manual tuning.

---

## Architecture

```
WAV/IQ/SigMF → Normalize → Spectral → SNR → CFO → Symbol Rate → Features
    → Classify Modulation → Costas Loop → Gardner TED → Demap
    → FEC Decode → Sync Correlate → Frame Extract → JSON Report
```

**12-stage pipeline** built on pure Python DSP (NumPy/SciPy), with a PySide6 + pyqtgraph GUI.

## Features

| Feature | Details |
|---------|---------|
| **File I/O** | WAV, raw IQ (cf32/cf64/ci16/ci8), SigMF |
| **Spectral Analysis** | Welch PSD, spectrogram, bandwidth estimation |
| **SNR Estimation** | M2M4 + spectral methods |
| **Parameter Extraction** | CFO (power-of-N + autocorrelation), symbol rate (cyclostationary) |
| **Modulation Classification** | Random Forest (92.5% CV accuracy) + heuristic fallback |
| **Supported Modulations** | BPSK, QPSK, 8PSK, 16QAM, 2FSK, 4FSK |
| **Demodulation** | Costas loop, Gardner TED, hard-decision demapper |
| **FEC Decoding** | Viterbi (K=7, R=1/2), Reed-Solomon RS(255,223) |
| **Sync Detection** | CCSDS ASM, Barker-7/11/13, auto-detect |
| **Grid Search** | Brute-force FEC × deinterleaver optimization |
| **Export** | JSON reports, session save/load (.npz) |
| **GUI** | Waterfall, PSD, constellation, eye diagram, bit viewer |

## Quick Start

### Prerequisites
- Python 3.11+
- Windows / Linux / macOS

### Install

```bash
# Clone and set up virtual environment
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\activate    # Windows
# source .venv/bin/activate  # Linux/macOS

# Install dependencies
pip install -e ".[dev]"
```

### Run Tests

```bash
set PYTHONPATH=src        # Windows
# export PYTHONPATH=src   # Linux/macOS
python -m pytest tests/ -v
```

### Generate Demo Signals

```bash
python -m siggen.test_suite --dataset demo
```

### Train ML Classifier (Optional)

A pre-trained model is included. To retrain:

```bash
python -m sigint_tool.ml.train_classifier -n 50
```

### Launch GUI

```bash
python -c "from sigint_tool.gui.main_window import main; main()"
```

### Build Standalone Executable

```bash
pip install pyinstaller
pyinstaller sigint_tool.spec
# Output: dist/SIGINTool/SIGINTool.exe
```

## Project Structure

```
.wav/
├── siggen/                          # Synthetic signal generator (test oracle)
│   ├── generator.py                 # End-to-end orchestrator
│   ├── modulator.py                 # BPSK/QPSK/8PSK/16QAM/2FSK/4FSK
│   ├── channel.py                   # AWGN, CFO, multipath, jitter
│   ├── fec_encoder.py               # Convolutional + Reed-Solomon
│   ├── interleaver.py               # Block + convolutional
│   └── framer.py                    # Sync words + headers + CRC
├── src/sigint_tool/
│   ├── core/                        # Pipeline framework
│   │   ├── signal_record.py         # Central data structure
│   │   └── pipeline.py              # Stage execution engine
│   ├── ingestion/                   # File readers + normalization
│   ├── analysis/                    # Spectral, SNR, CFO, symbol rate, features, classifier
│   ├── demod/                       # Costas loop, Gardner TED, demapper
│   ├── decode/                      # Viterbi, RS, de-interleavers, grid search
│   ├── correlation/                 # Sync word correlator + frame parser
│   ├── export/                      # JSON report + session save/load
│   ├── ml/                          # Classifier training script
│   └── gui/                         # PySide6 + pyqtgraph GUI
│       ├── main_window.py           # 3-panel dark-theme main window
│       ├── waterfall_widget.py      # Spectrogram waterfall
│       ├── psd_widget.py            # Power spectral density plot
│       ├── constellation_widget.py  # IQ scatter diagram
│       ├── eye_diagram_widget.py    # Overlaid eye diagram
│       └── bit_viewer_widget.py     # Hex + binary display
├── tests/                           # 99 unit tests
├── models/                          # Trained ML models (.joblib)
└── sigint_tool.spec                 # PyInstaller build spec
```

## Demo Workflow

1. **Generate** a synthetic QPSK signal with FEC encoding:
   ```bash
   python -c "
   from siggen.generator import SignalConfig, generate_signal
   cfg = SignalConfig(mod_type='QPSK', fec_type='viterbi', snr_db=15)
   result = generate_signal(cfg)
   import scipy.io.wavfile as wav
   import numpy as np
   iq = np.column_stack([result.signal.real, result.signal.imag])
   wav.write('demo_qpsk.wav', int(cfg.sample_rate), (iq * 32767).astype(np.int16))
   print('Generated demo_qpsk.wav')
   "
   ```

2. **Launch** the GUI and open the generated file

3. **Run Pipeline** (F5) — the tool will automatically:
   - Detect modulation → QPSK (92%+ confidence)
   - Extract CFO, symbol rate
   - Demodulate and decode
   - Find sync words and extract frames

4. **Export** JSON report (Ctrl+E) or save session (Ctrl+S)

Phase 1 (Ingestion):     17 tests
Phase 2 (Extraction):    16 tests
Phase 3-5 (Demod/Decode): 17 tests
Phase 6 (Integration):   11 tests
```

# Automated RF Signal Analysis System

A **hypothesis-driven, self-verifying, probabilistic** RF signal analysis engine that automatically recovers modulation, interleaving, Forward Error Correction (FEC), and framing structure from raw `.iq` and `.wav` signal recordings — without prior knowledge of transmitter parameters.

---

## Architecture Overview

```
Raw Signal File (.iq / .wav)
  │
  ▼
1. INGESTION & CONDITIONING
   ├── 11-Criterion Format Scorer (cf32/ci16/cs8, LE/BE, interleaved/planar)
   ├── Evidence-Driven DC Removal (gated at 2% DC fraction)
   └── Threshold-Gated Gram-Schmidt I/Q Imbalance Correction (5% threshold, 1D guard)
  │
  ▼
2. SPECTRAL CHARACTERIZATION
   ├── Welch PSD & CFAR Emission Detection (emission-bounded BW & carrier)
   ├── Modulation-Agnostic Spectral SNR (P_signal - P_noise_floor)
   └── Energy-Detector Burst Slicing & CUSUM Thresholding
  │
  ▼
3. PARAMETER ESTIMATION
   ├── Carrier Centering & Band-limited Filtering
   ├── Oerder-Meyr Cyclic FFT Symbol Rate Estimation (SPS)
   └── M-th Power / Spectral Line Carrier Frequency Offset (CFO)
  │
  ▼
4. AUTOMATIC MODULATION CLASSIFICATION (AMC)
   ├── Matched RRC Filtering with Symbol Phase Search
   ├── Higher-Order Cumulants (C40, C42) + Phase-Variance Check (8PSK vs FSK)
   └── Ranked Hypothesis Generation (BPSK, QPSK, 8PSK, 16-QAM, 64-QAM, 2-FSK, 4-FSK)
  │
  ▼
5. PROBABILISTIC HYPOTHESIS ORCHESTRATOR (Beam-Search)
   ├── Gardner Timing Recovery with State Continuity (no sample truncation)
   ├── Costas Loop Carrier Phase Recovery (bypassed for FSK frequency modulation)
   ├── Vectorized Soft-Decision LLR Demapper (scaled by noise variance 2σ²)
   ├── GF(2) Rank-Deficiency Matrix Interleaver Detector & Deinterleaver
   ├── Soft Viterbi (K=7, Rate-1/2) & Reed-Solomon GF(256) Codec with Forney Algorithm
   └── Re-encode Consistency Verification & Parity-Check Gating (≥85% threshold)
  │
  ▼
6. BITSTREAM & FRAME SYNCHRONIZATION
   ├── FFT Autocorrelation Frame Length Detector
   └── 256-Symbol Byte-Level Shannon Entropy Boundary Segmentation
  │
  ▼
7. FULL-STACK ANALYST WORKSTATION
   ├── FastAPI High-Performance Asynchronous REST API (Port 8000)
   └── Modern React + TypeScript + Tailwind + Recharts Interactive Web UI (Port 5173)
```

---

## Quick Start Guide

### Prerequisites
- **Python**: 3.10 or newer (tested on Python 3.10 – 3.14)
- **Node.js**: v18 or newer & **npm**

---

### Step 1: Clone & Setup Backend

```bash
# Navigate to the repository root
cd PS147

# Create and activate a virtual environment
python3 -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate    # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate

# Install Python dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

---

### Step 2: Setup Frontend

```bash
# Navigate to frontend directory and install dependencies
cd frontend
npm install
cd ..
```

---

### Step 3: Run the Application

#### Option A: Running in Two Terminals (Recommended for Development)

**Terminal 1 — Start the Backend Server (FastAPI on Port 8000):**
```bash
source venv/bin/activate
python -m uvicorn api.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --reload
```

**Terminal 2 — Start the Frontend Dev Server (Vite on Port 5173):**
```bash
cd frontend
npm run dev -- --host 0.0.0.0 --port 5173
```

#### Option B: Quick Start via Python Launcher
```bash
source venv/bin/activate
python run.py
```

Open your browser and navigate to:
👉 **[http://localhost:5173](http://localhost:5173)** (Web Workstation UI)
👉 **[http://localhost:8000/docs](http://localhost:8000/docs)** (Interactive Swagger API Documentation)

---

## Web Workstation UI Features

1. **Raw IQ Ingestion & Datatype Selector**:
   - Explicit selection for `cf32_le`, `ci16_le`, `cs8`, etc.
   - Ambiguity warning badge and confidence indicator whenever automatic detection is uncertain.
   - User sample rate configuration.
2. **Spectral & Time-Domain Analysis**:
   - **Interactive PSD Spectrum** with detected CFAR emission band overlay.
   - **Spectrogram / Waterfall Plot** showing frequency evolution over time.
   - **Time-Domain I/Q Oscilloscope** with instantaneous amplitude envelope.
   - **Constellation Diagram** (I vs Q scatter plot) for phase cluster diagnostics.
3. **Hypothesis Explorer & Beam Search**:
   - Ranked hypotheses with composite confidence scores and stage decomposition (`amc_margin`, `rank_drop`, `fec_syndrome_ratio`).
   - Uncertainty classification: **Aleatoric** (noise-dominated) vs. **Epistemic** (parameter ambiguity).
4. **Self-Verifying Payload & Framing**:
   - 4-State Payload status badges:
     - `✓ Recovered Payload` (Syndrome validated with re-encode match $\ge 85\%$)
     - `Candidate Framed Data`
     - `Candidate Bitstream`
     - `Raw Demodulated Bits`
   - Hex / ASCII payload viewer with frame delimiter lines and byte entropy metrics.
5. **Interactive Synthetic Signal Generator**:
   - Generate test files directly from the UI or API with customizable modulation, SNR (-5 dB to +30 dB), FEC, interleaver, and sample rate.

---

## API Endpoints

### `POST /api/analyze`
Upload a raw `.iq` or `.wav` file for characterization.

**Form Data Parameters:**
- `file` (File, required): Raw IQ binary file or WAV container.
- `iq_datatype` (str, optional): `cf32_le` | `ci16_le` | `cs8` | `auto`.
- `sample_rate` (float, optional): Sample rate in Hz (e.g. `1000000` for 1 MHz).
- `modulation_override` (str, optional): Force AMC modulation.
- `sps_override` (float, optional): Force samples per symbol.
- `cfo_override` (float, optional): Force CFO compensation in Hz.

**Response Structure (JSON):**
```json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "metadata": {
    "datatype": "cf32_le",
    "datatype_confidence": 1.0,
    "format_candidates": {"cf32_le": 0.95, "ci16_le": 0.12},
    "sample_rate": 1000000
  },
  "spectral": {
    "carrier": 1560.67,
    "bandwidth": 222656.25,
    "snr_db": 24.4,
    "emission": {
      "detected": true,
      "bw_emission": 296875.0,
      "bw_3db": 93750.0,
      "noise_floor_db": -52.3
    }
  },
  "estimation": {
    "sps": 8.0,
    "cfo_normalized": 0.0
  },
  "amc": [
    {"modulation": "QPSK", "order": 4, "confidence": 0.95}
  ],
  "hypotheses": [
    {
      "hypothesis_id": "hyp_0",
      "modulation": "QPSK",
      "confidence": 1.0,
      "payload_status": "validated_payload",
      "interleaver_state": "not_evaluated",
      "scores": {
        "fec_syndrome_ratio": 0.93,
        "decoder_path_quality": 0.95
      },
      "decoded_bits_hex": "76a5...",
      "decoded_bits_count": 2304
    }
  ]
}
```

### `POST /api/generate`
Generate a synthetic test signal with known ground truth parameters.

### `GET /api/health`
Health check endpoint returning API status and version.

---

## Running the Automated Test Suite

The test suite validates every layer against ground truth parameters with strict mathematical checks:

```bash
# Run all tests
venv/bin/pytest tests/ -v

# Run with test coverage
venv/bin/pytest tests/ --cov=core
```

**Test Coverage Areas:**
- `test_amc.py`: HOC cumulants calculation and FSK vs. 8PSK phase variance separation.
- `test_fec.py`: Viterbi soft decode bit-exact recovery, re-encode validation gate, full Reed-Solomon Forney multi-byte error correction, and blind convolutional search.
- `test_ingestion.py`: 11-criterion format scorer, 1D/2D guarded Gram-Schmidt IQ imbalance, DC removal, clipping detection.
- `test_interleaving.py`: GF(2) rank deficiency sweep and block de-interleaver matrix inversion.
- `test_pipeline_e2e.py`: End-to-end characterization pipeline across BPSK, QPSK, and 16-QAM signals.
- `test_spectral.py`: Welch PSD, CFAR emission detection, spectral SNR, burst detection.

---

## Key DSP Algorithms

1. **Evidence-Driven Conditioning**:
   - DC Offset is removed only when $|\text{DC}|/\text{RMS} > 2\%$.
   - Gram-Schmidt amplitude/phase balancing is gated at $5\%$ severity and guards against 1D signals ($P_I/P_Q > 4.0$).
2. **CFAR Emission Bounding**:
   - Noise floor is computed from the lower 25th spectral percentile.
   - 6 dB guard threshold identifies contiguous emission boundaries; carrier centroid and 3 dB bandwidth are computed strictly inside the detected emission band.
3. **Matched RRC Filtering & AMC**:
   - Oversampled signals are filtered using a root-raised-cosine matched filter, scanning symbol phases to evaluate cumulants at maximum constellation eye opening.
4. **Full Reed-Solomon Codec with Forney Algorithm**:
   - Computes error locator polynomial $\Lambda(x)$ via Berlekamp-Massey and roots via Chien search.
   - Evaluates error evaluator $\Omega(x) = [S(x)\Lambda(x)] \pmod{x^{2t}}$ and formal derivative $\Lambda'(x)$ to correct arbitrary multi-value GF(256) byte errors.
5. **Arbitrary-Length Stream Resilience**:
   - Inlined Gardner loop and trellis routines process signals of arbitrary length (tested on $>230,000$ samples / $>57,000$ bits) with zero sample truncation and sub-second performance.

---

│   ├── fec/                     # Viterbi, Reed-Solomon (Forney), LDPC, blind search

```

readme:
# RF Signal Intelligence

A GUI tool that takes a raw radio recording (`.wav` or `.IQ`), works out how the signal
was built, and decodes the message inside it — sampling rate, modulation, interleaving
and error-correction code are all identified automatically.

Runs entirely offline on a laptop. Pure Python: no GPU, no internet, no licensed software.

---

## Quick start (Windows)

Needs Python 3.10 or newer ([python.org](https://www.python.org/downloads/); tick
"Add Python to PATH" during install).

```
cd C:\Users\<you>\...\26147
python -m venv venv
venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

python scripts\generate_samples.py     # writes 7 test recordings into samples\
streamlit run app.py                   # opens the GUI in your browser
```

Run `venv\Scripts\activate` in every new Command Prompt. Stop the GUI with Ctrl+C.

To check the whole pipeline from the command line instead:

```
python scripts\decode_samples.py                  # all 7 samples, PASS / FAIL each
python scripts\decode_samples.py sig05_hf_audio.wav   # one file, stage by stage
```

---

## What it does, against the problem statement

| Required | Status | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accept `.IQ` or `.wav` input | Yes — stereo WAV as I/Q, mono WAV as real passband, raw IQ as cf32 / ci16 / ci8 / cu8 (RTL-SDR) | `rfsig/io.py` |
| Identify sampling frequency | From the WAV header, a hint in the file name, or the analyst for headerless IQ | `rfsig/io.py` |
| Identify modulation | BPSK, QPSK, 8PSK, 16QAM, 2FSK, 4FSK, 8FSK | `rfsig/demod.py` |
| Identify FEC | Convolutional (K=3/5/7), Reed-Solomon, concatenated RS + convolutional, LDPC, or uncoded | `rfsig/identify.py`, `rfsig/fec.py` |
| Identify interleaving | Block, diagonal, convolutional (Forney), pseudo-random — including the exact size or seed | `rfsig/identify.py`, `rfsig/interleave.py` |
| Demodulate FSK / PSK / QAM | Matched filtering, timing recovery, carrier recovery, soft-decision output | `rfsig/demod.py` |
| De-interleave | All four families above | `rfsig/interleave.py` |
| FEC decoding | Viterbi (soft decision), Reed-Solomon, concatenated, LDPC min-sum belief propagation | `rfsig/fec.py` |
| Bitstream correlation for header / payload | Sync-word cross-correlation plus a blind bit-constancy method | `rfsig/correlate.py` |
| Spectral features in a GUI | Spectrum, waterfall, constellation, eye diagram, tone clusters, symbol-rate line | `app.py` |

---

## The sample recordings

`python scripts\generate_samples.py` writes seven files that between them exercise every
stage. The true settings are recorded in `samples\manifest.json`.

| File | Modulation | Error correction | Interleaver | Format |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| sig01 | BPSK | Convolutional K=7 | Block 28×37 | .iq float32 |
| sig02 | QPSK | Reed-Solomon + convolutional | Convolutional B=8 J=4 | .iq int16 |
| sig03 | 8PSK | Convolutional K=5 | Diagonal 24×43 | stereo .wav (I/Q) |
| sig04 | 16QAM | Reed-Solomon | Pseudo-random, seed 42 | .iq float32 |
| sig05 | 2FSK | Convolutional K=3 | Block 4×257 | mono .wav (HF audio) |
| sig06 | 4FSK | LDPC | none | .iq float32 |
| sig07 | QPSK | none | none | .iq uint8 (RTL-SDR) |

Each carries the same hidden text message, split across 16 frames. Recovering that text
is the end-to-end proof that every stage worked.

---

## Using the GUI

**Sidebar** — pick a sample or upload your own recording. Raw `.iq` files have no header,
so the sample format and sampling rate are set here (pre-filled from the file name when it
contains something like `fs48000`). WAV files read their own header. "Ground truth" shows
the real settings of a sample so you can compare.

**Signal parameters** — sampling rate, symbol rate, modulation, decision SNR, occupied
bandwidth, carrier offset, samples per symbol, duration. The analysis log below lists what
each stage found, in order.

**Plot tabs**

| Tab | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| Spectrum | Power against frequency, with the occupied band and noise floor marked |
| Waterfall | Frequency against time, colour = power |
| Constellation | Symbols before carrier recovery (a spinning ring) and after (tight clusters on the ideal points) |
| Eye diagram | Overlaid symbol traces; an open eye means the timing is right |
| Tone clusters / Instantaneous frequency | For FSK: the separate tones, and the signal hopping between them |
| Symbol rate | The spectral line the symbol rate was measured from |

**Decoding tabs**

| Tab | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| Frame sync | Preamble correlation along the bitstream, one spike per frame, and which phase rotation was correct |
| Interleaver + FEC | The winning hypothesis, how many were tested, and a ranked chart of the runners-up |
| Decode quality | Bit error rate before correction, Reed-Solomon bytes repaired, LDPC iterations |
| Header / payload | Bit constancy across frames, the estimated header boundary, and parsed header fields per frame |
| Message | The recovered text |
| Export | Decoded bits, payload, and a JSON report |

---

## How it works

1. **Load.** Samples are converted to complex baseband. A mono WAV is treated as a real
   passband recording and turned into an analytic signal with the Hilbert transform.
2. **Measure.** Welch power spectral density gives the noise floor, the 99 % occupied
   bandwidth, the carrier offset and an SNR estimate.
3. **Symbol rate.** A digitally modulated signal repeats its statistics once per symbol,
   so a non-linear transform produces a spectral line exactly at the symbol rate: the
   squared envelope |x|² for PSK/QAM, the rate of frequency jumps for FSK.
4. **Modulation.** For linear modulations, raising the symbols to the power M leaves a
   tone only for the matching scheme (M=2 for BPSK, 4 for QPSK and 16QAM, 8 for 8PSK);
   QPSK and 16QAM are separated by the noise-corrected C42 cumulant and amplitude spread.
   FSK is identified by clustering the instantaneous frequency into equally spaced tones.
5. **Demodulate.** Root-raised-cosine matched filter, Oerder & Meyr feed-forward timing
   recovery (block-wise, so clock drift is tracked), carrier recovery from the M-th power
   line plus a Viterbi & Viterbi phase estimator, then soft (log-likelihood) demapping.
   FSK uses a non-coherent tone filter bank.
6. **Frame sync.** The 48-bit preamble is cross-correlated along the bitstream. Because a
   PSK/QAM receiver cannot tell which constellation point is "north", every rotation and a
   spectrum flip are tried and the preamble picks the winner. With no known preamble the
   tool finds the frame period from the bitstream autocorrelation and the preamble from
   bit positions that stay constant across frames.
7. **Identify interleaver and code.** Every plausible interleaver (matrix shapes,
   convolutional B/J settings, pseudo-random seeds) is applied, and each result is scored
   against every candidate code using algebraic structure: the rate-1/2 parity relation
   c1·g2 + c2·g1 = 0 for convolutional codes, syndromes and Berlekamp-Massey error-locator
   length for Reed-Solomon, unsatisfied parity checks for LDPC. Wrong guesses score near
   zero, so the right one stands out. Thousands of hypotheses are checked in about a second.
8. **Decode.** Soft-decision Viterbi, Reed-Solomon, concatenated (inner Viterbi then outer
   RS) or LDPC min-sum belief propagation.
9. **Correlate.** The frame sync word is located by cross-correlation, the header fields
   parsed, and the payload extracted. Independently, stacking the frames and measuring how
   often each bit position repeats reveals the header/payload boundary without knowing the
   format at all.

---

## Test results

| Test | Result |
| --- | --- |
| The 7 sample recordings (`scripts\decode_samples.py`) | 7 / 7 — modulation, interleaver, code and message all correct |
| 42 random configurations across every modulation, code and interleaver, 9–25 dB SNR, including 7 in blind mode | 42 / 42 |
| Blind mode (unknown preamble), 9 targeted cases | 9 / 9 |

Typical analysis time is 1–5 seconds per recording on a laptop.

---

## Limits and honest notes

- The tool recognises the code families listed above with the parameters it knows. A real
  deployment would carry a larger library (other rates, puncturing, DVB/802.11 LDPC tables).
  Adding a code means adding an encoder, a decoder and a structure test in `rfsig/fec.py`.
- A raw `.IQ` file carries no sampling rate. The tool takes it from the file name or from
  the analyst; everything downstream is measured relative to it.
- Blind mode (unknown preamble) is slower because it must also guess where frames begin.
  A pseudo-random interleaver in blind mode can take minutes.
- Very low SNR (below about 8 dB for BPSK, more for higher-order schemes) breaks
  identification, as it would for any receiver.
- Signals are analysed offline from a file. There is no live SDR capture path.

---

## Project layout

```
app.py                      Streamlit GUI
requirements.txt            Python dependencies
rfsig/                      the analysis library
  io.py                     file loading (.wav, raw .iq)
  params.py                 spectrum, bandwidth, SNR, symbol rate
  modem.py                  constellations, Gray mapping, pulse shaping
  demod.py                  modulation ID and demodulation
  framing.py                frame synchronisation
  interleave.py             the four interleaver families
  fec.py                    convolutional/Viterbi, Reed-Solomon, concatenated, LDPC
  identify.py               blind interleaver + code identification
  correlate.py              sync word, header/payload
  pipeline.py               runs the stages end to end
  generator.py              synthetic transmitter used to make test signals
  utils.py                  bit helpers and constants
scripts/
  generate_samples.py       writes the 7 sample recordings
  decode_samples.py         decodes them and checks against the ground truth
docs/
  system-architecture.html  interactive architecture diagram
  analyst-workflow.html     interactive user-workflow diagram
samples/                    generated recordings + manifest.json (ground truth)
```

Dependencies: numpy, scipy, reedsolo, streamlit, plotly. Everything else — Viterbi
decoding, LDPC, the interleavers, the identification search — is implemented in this
repository.

---

## Demo script (about 3 minutes)

1. **Open `sig01_fs48000.iq`.** Say: this is a raw recording, no metadata at all. Point at
   the parameter row — bandwidth, symbol rate and modulation were all measured from the
   samples.
2. **Constellation tab.** Left plot is a ring: the receiver has not locked the carrier yet.
   Right plot snaps onto two BPSK points. That is demodulation working.
3. **Interleaver + FEC tab.** 1,859 hypotheses tested. The right answer scores 1.00; the
   next best scores 0.24. Nobody told the tool the code — it proved it.
4. **Message tab.** The text comes out. Every stage had to be right for this to read.
5. **Switch to `sig04`** (pseudo-random interleaver, seed 42) and say: this one was
   scrambled with a secret seed; the tool searched 256 of them and found it in about a
   second.
6. **Switch to `sig05_hf_audio.wav`** and say: this is not I/Q at all, it is audio from an
   HF receiver, and the same pipeline decodes it.
